Nxeon platform (/opt/nxeon), a VPS/game hosting business with a live-chat AI support widget. A real customer just asked the chat AI "How can I make a free minecraft server on it" and the AI replied claiming "there's no free Minecraft server option on Nxeon," recommending the customer port-forward their home internet instead, and listing paid Minecraft tiers ($4.99/mo, $8.99/mo) as the only options.

This is factually WRONG. Per this platform's own history, there IS a real, live free Minecraft tier: a `freemc-host` VM running Docker + mc-router (subdomain-based routing with auto-sleep/wake, like Aternos), shipped live on 2026-08-24, plus a real customer-facing free-MC management dashboard (power/console/players/settings/presets/rename/change-domain) shipped the same day. This is a real, working, currently-live product feature — not vaporware — yet the chat AI told a paying-potential customer it doesn't exist.

I need you to find the root cause of why the chat AI doesn't know this feature exists, and fix it. Steps:

1. Find the live-chat AI agent's code — likely something like `lib/chat-agent.ts`, `app/api/chat/`, or similar (search for "chat agent", "live chat", "site widget" in the codebase). This underwent a "flagship rework" in a past session (tool loop for everyone, no blog-dump fallback) — find that implementation.
2. Determine HOW the chat agent currently knows about (or fails to know about) Nxeon's product catalog/features when answering customer questions — does it have a system prompt describing available products? Does it call a tool to query the real GamePlan/hosting catalog? Does it have any knowledge specifically about the free Minecraft tier (`freemc-host`, or however it's represented in the DB/catalog — check for a special product type, flag, or route like `/freemc` or similar; check prisma schema for any free-tier-specific model or flag)?
3. Identify EXACTLY why "free minecraft" queries fail to surface the real feature — e.g., is the free-MC product simply missing from whatever catalog/tool-context the chat agent uses (since it might be a special standalone system separate from the normal paid GamePlan catalog, and was never added to the chat agent's knowledge/tools when it shipped on 2026-08-24, likely because the chat agent rework and the free-MC feature happened as separate initiatives that never got cross-wired)? Confirm this hypothesis or find the real cause.
4. Fix it: make sure the chat agent can accurately answer questions about the free Minecraft tier — how to get one, what it includes (2GB Aternos-style with auto-sleep/wake, subdomain routing), and correctly direct customers to it (check the actual customer-facing entry point/URL/dashboard tab for creating a free MC server — the admin's own manual reply to this customer said "Go to My Services, and then Free services tab", so confirm that's the real path and make sure the chat agent's guidance matches reality).
5. Also double check: is there any other similarly-live, real Nxeon feature that might have the same blind spot (shipped outside the chat agent's normal catalog-sync path)? Just note if you spot one, don't go fix unrelated things — stay focused on the free-MC gap.
6. Test the fix for real — actually invoke the chat agent (however it's normally tested/invoked in this repo, check for existing test files or an admin test-chat interface) with a similar "how do I get a free minecraft server" question and confirm it now gives an accurate answer.
7. Deploy through the normal pipeline: commit -> push -> deploy-staging.sh -> verify HTTP 200 -> promote-production.sh -> verify HTTP 200 AND a genuinely fresh BUILD_ID (compare against current value first).

Do NOT reply to the live customer chat yourself (Raunit Kumar / kriruchi121@gmail.com) — the admin already handled that conversation manually. This task is strictly about fixing the underlying chat-agent knowledge gap in code, not sending any message to any customer.

Report back concisely: root cause found, what you changed, how you verified the chat agent now answers correctly, and confirmation of production deploy with a fresh BUILD_ID.

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# next.config sets output:"standalone" but the systemd unit runs the standalone
# server.js directly (not `next start`, which Next.js explicitly does not
# support alongside output:"standalone" — it prints a warning and silently
# fails to resolve some routes, confirmed live 2026-09-10: a brand-new API
# route 404'd under `next start` on this exact build and returned 200 under
# `node .next/standalone/server.js`). The standalone output does NOT include
# public/ or .next/static/ (Next's own documented behavior) — copy them in
# fresh every build, or every static asset/route added after the last copy
# is missing until the next deploy happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle on purpose, since it reads .dat files off its own package path at
# runtime) — but the standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace
# as JS-imported, so an externalized package's own non-JS data files are
# silently left behind. Found live 2026-09-10: this crashed EVERY request
# with an uncaught ENOENT the moment the systemd unit ran the standalone
# server.js instead of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around
# geoip.lookup() does NOT help, because the failure isn't confined to that
# call. Copy the package's real data/ directory in every build, same
# reasoning as public/.next/static above.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
echo "==> Staging responds: HTTP $CODE (http://$(grep ^PUBLIC_IP .env | cut -d= -f2):8080)"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "STAGING UNHEALTHY"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Staging deploy complete"

#!/bin/bash
# Promote the currently deployed staging commit to production.
# Verifies staging is healthy, fast-forwards nothing (prod working tree IS the repo),
# then rebuilds + restarts production services.
set -euo pipefail

STG_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon-staging rev-parse HEAD)
PROD_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon rev-parse HEAD)

echo "==> Staging is at:    $STG_COMMIT"
echo "==> Production is at: $PROD_COMMIT"

if ! systemctl is-active -q nxeon-staging-web; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging web service is not running." >&2
  exit 1
fi
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
if [ "$CODE" != "200" ]; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging returns HTTP $CODE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$STG_COMMIT" != "$PROD_COMMIT" ]; then
  echo "Note: production tree is at a different commit than staging."
  echo "Production deploys directly from /opt/nxeon's working tree (main)."
fi

cd /opt/nxeon
echo "==> Installing dependencies (adds any new deps before build)"
# CRITICAL: without this, a commit that adds a new dependency (e.g. imapflow)
# builds against a stale node_modules and fails — which previously aborted the
# promote AFTER the old build was already gone. Always sync deps first.
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3
# CRITICAL: this was previously `prisma generate` only — regenerates the
# CLIENT's types (fixes the build) but never touches the actual DATABASE.
# Staging and production are SEPARATE databases (nxeon_staging vs nxeon, same
# Postgres server, confirmed live) — deploy-staging.sh's own `db push` only
# ever applies to staging's DB, so a schema change promoted this way built
# and deployed fine while production's actual table never got the new
# column, silently breaking the FIRST thing that queried it post-deploy
# (found live 2026-09-02: worker/billing.ts's sweeps started throwing
# "column does not exist" immediately after a routine promote — no staging
# failure gave any warning, since staging's own db push had already
# succeeded there). `db push` both applies the schema AND regenerates the
# client, so this replaces the old generate-only step rather than adding a
# second one. Schema changes are rare enough that this always running
# unconditionally costs nothing when there's nothing new to push.
echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss --schema=/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma 2>&1 | tail -4
echo "==> Building production"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4
# Guard: never restart into an incomplete/failed build. A valid production build
# always writes .next/BUILD_ID; if it's missing the build failed mid-way and the
# old in-memory process is still serving — abort rather than kill it.
if [ ! -s /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID ]; then
  echo "BUILD FAILED: .next/BUILD_ID missing — NOT restarting (old process left serving)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
# next.config sets output:"standalone"; the standalone server.js is what the
# systemd unit actually runs (not `next start` — see deploy-staging.sh's own
# comment on this same step for the 2026-09-10 incident). Its output does NOT
# include public/ or .next/static/ (Next's documented behavior) — refresh
# them every promote, same as staging, or new/changed static assets are
# missing from prod until the next promote happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle since it reads .dat files off its own package path at runtime) — the
# standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace as JS-imported, so
# an externalized package's own non-JS data files are silently left behind.
# Found live 2026-09-10 on staging: this crashes EVERY request with an
# uncaught ENOENT the moment something runs the standalone server.js instead
# of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around geoip.lookup() does NOT
# help, the failure isn't confined to that call. Copy the real data/
# directory every promote, same reasoning as public/.next/static above. This
# has NOT yet bitten production because nxeon-web's systemd unit still runs
# `npm start` (next start) today, not server.js directly — but this fix must
# land before that switch happens, not after.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi
# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. .next needs to be writable by it
# (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable. .env is the one
# exception: systemd's EnvironmentFile= reads it as root (PID 1, pre-privilege
# drop) so the app's process env is fine either way, but Prisma's generated
# client ALSO opens .env directly at Client instantiation to resolve its own
# env() directives — that read happens as the actual 'nxeon' process user, so
# a root-owned .env throws EACCES there on every cold start (harmless once
# systemd's injected vars are already in process.env, but noisy, and a prior
# root-run edit to this file silently reverted the ownership fix below once
# already — confirmed live 2026-09-02). Keep .env nxeon-owned, not world- or
# group-readable. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next/.env ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chown nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true
echo "==> Restarting production web"
systemctl restart nxeon-web

# Drain in-flight provisions before bouncing the worker. Restarting the worker
# mid-provision used to interrupt a live VM build and (with a non-idempotent retry)
# strand the server in ERROR. The start step is now idempotent so this is
# belt-and-suspenders, but avoiding the interruption entirely is cleaner. Bounded
# wait (max ~4 min) so a deploy can never hang forever.
DBURL=$(grep -E '^DATABASE_URL=' /opt/nxeon/.env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"')
if [ -n "$DBURL" ] && command -v psql >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for _ in $(seq 1 24); do
    ACTIVE=$(psql "$DBURL" -tAc "SELECT count(*) FROM \"Job\" WHERE status='RUNNING' AND type='PROVISION';" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
    [ "${ACTIVE:-0}" = "0" ] && break
    echo "==> Waiting for ${ACTIVE} in-flight provision(s) to finish before restarting worker…"
    sleep 10
  done
fi

echo "==> Restarting production worker"
systemctl restart nxeon-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-web nxeon-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1/)
echo "==> Production responds: HTTP $CODE"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "PRODUCTION UNHEALTHY — check journalctl -u nxeon-web"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Production promote complete"
